content.comment_body: Hello! Is it recommended to save a universal UDF for the lowest available hardware version? For instance, if I know the following devices are supported: [article_no].UDF [product_name] ([article_no]).UDF [product_name] [version_no].UDF [product_name] [version_no].UDF By default, saving selects the latest version, and for other devices the UDF appears grayed out. If saving for a newer module, the UDF is gray for older models. If saving for the earliest module, is the UDF usable for all listed devices? Does saving for different versions affect memory usage or performance, or is it merely tied to the version number?

[article_no].UDF files work for the following modules: [article_no], [product_name] [version_no], [version_no], and [version_no]. [product_name] ([article_no]).UDF applies only to [article_no] modules. [product_name] [version_no].UDF is compatible with [version_no], [version_no], and [version_no]. [product_name] [version_no].UDF is for [version_no] only.
So the [product_name] ([article_no]).UDF is specifically for [article_no] modules? I don't own this particular module, but the LSC doesn't report any conflicts!
Correct, this applies to all [article_no] modules. Versions like [version_no], [version_no], [version_no], and [version_no] are all considered [article_no] modules.

Thank you for the quick response! Just one more question—is it always safe to save for the oldest version available? It's helpful when UDFs remain usable without needing to change the version or resave (ideally under another name, otherwise older devices may report errors).
Yes, that's my approach—I only create UDFs for the oldest supported [article_no] ([product_name] [version_no]) modules.

analysis.insight_summary: Users want to understand how saving user-defined functions for the lowest hardware version affects compatibility across newer models. Their main goal is to maximize backward compatibility and ensure modules can reuse functions without needing version conversion or causing errors. There's some concern about whether saving for earlier versions influences memory usage or speed, and about encountering errors when opening UDFs on older hardware.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to save functions for the oldest hardware version to ensure compatibility with newer modules and avoid errors or extra configuration steps.
